Dogo uses accessibility for two things.

Gestures: to lock your phone or open Recents when you use a gesture.

Phone use: only after you approve a task in Dogo, it can read the screen of the one app you chose and tap, type and scroll in it. It stops when you press Stop, when the task ends, or when the screen locks. It never reads password fields, and it does not watch what you do the rest of the time.
To improve app suggestions, turn on usage access for %1$s
To access shortcuts and additional features, set Dogo as your default launcher
At a Glance can be added to the home screen with the Dogo widget
To put the device to sleep, set Dogo as a device admin app. Tap \"Open settings\", then tap \"Activate this device admin app.\"
To %1$s, turn on the Dogo accessibility service. Tap \"Open settings\", choose \"Dogo\" and turn on \"Use Dogo.\"

Dogo uses Accessibility\'s `performGlobalAction` method to perform this action. This is a sensitive permission that allows monitoring other apps. However, Dogo is not configured for that functionality and receives no events.
